The Story of Dhridh-surya

I bow to Lord Jina, who illuminates the world through omniscience and reveals the true nature of all things, and who is worshipped by the king of gods. I write the story of Dhridh-surya, which bestows faith upon living beings.

This story is set in the time when Dhanpal was king of Ujjayini, a renowned ruler among the kings of his era. His chief queen was Dhanvati. One day Dhanvati went to the royal garden with her companions to enjoy the spring beauty. Around her neck hung a necklace of very precious gems. A courtesan named Vasantsena, who had also come to the garden, saw it and her heart became consumed with desire for it. Without it, life seemed meaningless to her. She returned home sorrowful and remained despondent all day.

When her lover Dhridh-surya came that evening and saw her unhappy, he asked, "Beloved, tell me quickly — why are you displeased today?" Vasantsena, seeing him so concerned, said, "Today I went to the garden and saw a beautiful necklace on the queen's neck. If you bring it to me, only then can I live, and only then can you be my true lover."

Dhridh-surya set out for the necklace. He went straight to the palace and by fortune managed to steal it. As he left the palace, the guards caught him immediately. At dawn he was brought before the royal court. The king sentenced him to death by impalement. He was placed upon the stake. At that very moment, a merchant named Dhandatt was on his way to the Jain temple for worship. Dhridh-surya, judging from the merchant's face and bearing that he was a compassionate man, called out, "Sethji, you are a great devotee of Lord Jina and a kind soul. I beg of you — I am terribly thirsty. Please bring me a little water to drink, and you shall earn great merit."

Dhandatt, wishing to do him good, said, "Brother, I shall bring water, but in the meantime you must do one thing for me. Through twelve years of hard labour, by my guru's grace, I have learned a certain sacred science. If I go to fetch water and forget it in the meantime, all my effort will be wasted and I shall suffer great loss. So I entrust it to you — I shall teach you the mantra, and you must hold it in your mind until I return." Dhridh-surya agreed, and the merchant taught him the sacred Panch Namaskar Mantra.

Dhridh-surya began to recite the mantra with devotion, even as he hung upon the stake. Through the power of the mantra and the sincerity of his recitation at the moment of death, his karmas were purified. When his life ended, he was reborn as a deity in heaven. The merchant returned with water to find that Dhridh-surya had already departed — but he had departed in a state of supreme peace, his mind filled with the sacred mantra.

This story teaches that even at the last moment of life, sincere faith and devotion can transform one's destiny. Dhridh-surya was a thief condemned to death, yet through the grace of a compassionate merchant and the power of the Namaskar Mantra, he attained a heavenly birth. No soul is beyond redemption; the door of grace remains open until the very last breath.
